candidates.reason: tcp_parse_options main walk: between consuming the kind byte (opcode = *ptr++) and the length byte (opsize = *ptr++ at line 4558) there is an explicit 'if (length < 2) return;' at line 4556; EOL returns, NOP decrements length before continue, so NOP bookkeeping is exact (one byte consumed, one byte decremented). opsize<2 and opsize>length both bail before ptr += opsize-2. No missing remaining>=2 check.
tcp_parse_mss_option has the same 'if (length < 2) return mss;' guard at line 4504 before opsize = *ptr++; NOP path length-- is exact; opsize>length rejects partial options before ptr advance.

mptcp_get_options contains the exact seed-fix guard: 'if (length < 2) return;' at line 386 between 'opcode = *ptr++' (line 378) and 'opsize = *ptr++' (line 388); NOP decrements length by exactly 1 per byte consumed; opsize<2 and opsize>length both return. The seed vulnerability shape is fixed in this tree.

tcp_do_parse_auth_options (TCP MD5/AO walk): default case reads 'opsize = *ptr++' with no literal length<2 check, but the loop condition is 'while (length >= minlen)' where minlen is TCPOLEN_MD5SIG (18) or sizeof(struct tcp_ao_hdr)+1 (>=19); after one opcode byte is consumed at least minlen-1 >= 17 bytes remain, so the second byte read is always in bounds; opsize<2 || opsize>length rejects before advance.

synproxy_parse_options has 'if (length < 2) return true;' at line 54 before 'opsize = *ptr++'; additionally length<0 is rejected and the whole option area is fetched via skb_header_pointer with a 40-byte stack buffer, so no OOB.
synproxy_tstamp_adjust walk checks 'optoff + 1 == optend || optoff + op[1] > optend || op[1] < 2' before using the length byte, equivalent remaining>=2 semantics.

tcp_options() ('Simplified tcp_parse_options routine') has 'if (length < 2) return;' at line 364; tcp_sack() at line 426 likewise; both copy options into a fixed (15*4-sizeof(tcphdr)) stack buffer via skb_header_pointer, bounding reads.

cake_get_tcpopt ('inspired by tcp_parse_options') has 'if (length < 2) break;' at line 1030 before opsize read; second walk at line 1169 also guarded; opsize<2 || opsize>length rejects partial options.
cookie_v6_check calls tcp_parse_options (guarded upstream); no independent option walk. Same for net/ipv4/syncookies.c:378 and net/ipv4/tcp_minisocks.c callers.

optlen() reads opt[offset] and opt[offset+1]; callers bound the loop: tcpmss_mangle_packet iterates 'for (i = sizeof(struct tcphdr); i <= tcp_hdrlen - TCPOLEN_MSS; i += optlen(opt, i))' and validates len>=tcp_hdrlen first, so i+1 < tcp_hdrlen always holds when optlen reads two bytes; TCPOPTSTRIP and nft_exthdr use 'i < tcp_hdrlen - 1' / 'i < tcphdr_len - 1' before optlen(), and reject i+optl > tcp_hdrlen.

tcp_accecn_process_option re-fetches the saved AccECN option via skb_transport_header + rx_opt.accecn (an offset saved by tcp_parse_options only for a fully in-bounds option) and guards with WARN_ON_ONCE on the kind byte; optlen derived from ptr[1]-2 of the validated option; indirect but bounded by the same validated header area.
